Not compliance, not FDA validation, not GxP validation or CSV, not 21 CFR Part 11 compliance, not certification, not an independent audit; Arc21 is not a regulated system. supportLevels.evidenced: the tested behaviour is what the statement describes and every cited record held (no deficient, no gap). Tested paths only — never a statement that the control is met.
supportLevels.partial: the evidence bears on part of what the statement asks, or cited records include deficient or gap results, or the relationship is an analogy. Every Part 11 provision and every activity of Attest itself is capped here.
supportLevels.not_mapped: no Attest evidence supports a mapping; nothing is cited as evidence.

mappings.title: Access Enforcement
statement: Enforce approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources in accordance with applicable access control policies.
mappings.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, release 5.2.0 — NIST's OSCAL catalog, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/usnistgov/oscal-content/main/nist.gov/SP800-53/rev5/json/NIST_SP-800-53_rev5_catalog.json
mappings.subject: arc21

artifacts.summary: WP1 harness validation (run `20260922T234324Z-5695a4c3df2d`): 5 of 5 deliberately broken controls detected and 5 restored; over-privileged connections told intact from broken in 0 of 10 checks; the testing login can switch into service_role.

mappings.relevance: AC-3 asks the system to enforce approved authorizations for logical access. For a client of Arc21 the enforcement point is PostgreSQL itself: table and column grants decide whether a role may touch a relation at all, and row-level policies decide which rows. The read-isolation, write-isolation, WITH CHECK, anonymous-exposure, column and Realtime families attempt — under role-scoped sessions carrying a real user's identity — exactly the reads and writes the approved WP3 matrix says must be refused or allowed, and the null-identity boundary rows make the same attempts with no identity at all.
demonstrates: 207 Test IDs, 207 effective, 0 deficient, 0 gap: on every direct path tested the database refused what the matrix forbids and allowed what it permits — another user's rows neither readable nor writable, no row attributable to another user, nothing reachable anonymously that the matrix forbids, columns outside the grant refused, Realtime topics admitting only their members.

The role scoping is load-bearing (WP1): in all 5 deliberate-break scenarios the role-scoped probe noticed the broken control, while the same statements on over-privileged connections could not tell an intact control from a broken one (0 of 10 checks discriminated).
doesNotDemonstrate: That the authorizations are "approved" by anyone but the author: the approved WP3 matrix is the author's own expectation set, and no organizational access-control policy stands behind it.
Enforcement inside SECURITY DEFINER functions, which happens in each function's body rather than in a policy — that is AC-6 and AC-24 below, where the open finding A4 sits.
Enforcement at the application or HTTP layer (out of scope, brief §4), or in platform schemas Arc21 does not own.
Anything about branches the matrix does not name, or about any other schema version than the one assessed.
limitations: One schema version (59 migrations, `5695a4c3df2d`), one disposable local instance, synthetic accounts. Each negative test simulates the attack its approved row names; nothing searched for others.
Not independent: the author wrote Arc21, the harness and the expectations.
mappings.arguable: Why AC-3 and not AC-6: these tests ask whether a request the rules forbid is refused — enforcement. Whether the rules themselves grant more than a role needs is AC-6's question. The column-level family bears on both and is listed under both.

mappings.title: Least Privilege
statement: Employ the principle of least privilege, allowing only authorized accesses for users (or processes acting on behalf of users) that are necessary to accomplish assigned organizational tasks.
mappings.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, release 5.2.0 — NIST's OSCAL catalog, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/usnistgov/oscal-content/main/nist.gov/SP800-53/rev5/json/NIST_SP-800-53_rev5_catalog.json

artifacts.summary: WP0 inventory (run `20260922T234324Z-5695a4c3df2d`): 40 resources, 397 (resource, control) pairs, 50 policies, 88 SECURITY DEFINER functions (55 callable by a client role), 16 roles (5 with BYPASSRLS); row-level security enabled on 39 of 39 tables and forced on 0.

WP1 harness validation (run `20260922T234324Z-5695a4c3df2d`): 5 of 5 deliberately broken controls detected and 5 restored; over-privileged connections told intact from broken in 0 of 10 checks; the testing login can switch into service_role.

mappings.relevance: AC-6 asks that users, and processes acting on their behalf, hold only the access their tasks need. Arc21's SECURITY DEFINER functions are such processes: each runs with its owner's privileges — the owner is postgres, which bypasses row-level security — on behalf of whichever client calls it. The definer-function family asks whether a client-callable function can be used to reach beyond the caller's own authority; the column family whether grants stop at the columns a role needs; the FORCE family records which roles sit outside row-level policy altogether.
demonstrates: Definer functions: 52 of 58 held; 5 did not — register_push_token reassigns another account's device registration to the caller (A4, open), and four leaderboard functions return a private-profile player's display name (A1, accepted by the author as design intent); 1 characterized (sprint standings, B2, accepted).
Column grants: 12 of 12 held.

FORCE / BYPASSRLS: 24 characterized records — row-level security is enabled but not forced on every High-tier table, the owner is postgres, and 5 roles on the instance hold BYPASSRLS (postgres, service_role, supabase_admin, supabase_etl_admin, supabase_read_only_user); the author classed this informational (B1).
WP0: 88 SECURITY DEFINER functions, 55 of them callable by a client role; one latent grant (realtime.messages grants INSERT, SELECT and UPDATE to anon, which no policy admits — B4, informational).

WP1: the login every control test uses can switch into service_role, which bypasses row-level security; what keeps the harness from testing as it is code in the harness, not a property of the database.
doesNotDemonstrate: That any privilege is necessary to accomplish an assigned task: there is no task or role analysis to compare the grants against.
Review of privileged accounts, or who holds the service-role credential: deployment and credential handling are unknown (RUBRIC 4.6).
The 32 server-only SECURITY DEFINER functions no test calls: they are not executable by a client role, so they are outside the definer-function family's question.
limitations: Each client-callable definer function was exercised on the escalation its approved row names — usually one path through its body, not all of them.
A4 is open; nothing was remediated (Amendment A1).
mappings.arguable: Why the definer functions map to AC-6 rather than AC-3: a definer function's refusal is written in its own body and runs with its owner's full privileges, so the question is whether that elevated privilege stays within what the caller may do — least privilege for a process acting on a user's behalf. A4 is where it does not. AC-24 covers the same functions from the decision side.

mappings.title: Access Control Decisions
statement: [Selection (one-or-more): establish procedures; implement mechanisms] to ensure [Assignment: access control decisions] are applied to each access request prior to access enforcement.
mappings.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, release 5.2.0 — NIST's OSCAL catalog, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/usnistgov/oscal-content/main/nist.gov/SP800-53/rev5/json/NIST_SP-800-53_rev5_catalog.json

artifacts.summary: WP0 inventory (run `20260922T234324Z-5695a4c3df2d`): 40 resources, 397 (resource, control) pairs, 50 policies, 88 SECURITY DEFINER functions (55 callable by a client role), 16 roles (5 with BYPASSRLS); row-level security enabled on 39 of 39 tables and forced on 0.

mappings.relevance: AC-24 separates the access-control decision from its enforcement and asks that the decision be applied to each access request before enforcement. In PostgreSQL row-level security the decision is a policy's USING or WITH CHECK expression, evaluated for every row a statement touches; WP0 read every one of those expressions from the catalog.
demonstrates: WP0: 50 policies, each with its USING and WITH CHECK expression as PostgreSQL prints it, read from the live catalog rather than from the migrations.
Read and write decisions applied per request on the direct table path: 69 of 69 held.

On another path the table's decision is not applied: SECURITY DEFINER functions that join public.profiles without its privacy and block decision (4 deficient, A1; 1 characterized, B2). The author accepted both as intended behaviour at CP4 (J1, J10); the records keep their verdicts.
doesNotDemonstrate: Organization-defined decisions: Arc21's decisions exist only as code (policies and function bodies) and as the approved matrix; nothing documents them as policy.
Decision logging, or a decision point separate from the database.
limitations: The records show the outcome of each decision for the tested identities and fixtures; they do not prove an expression correct for every input.
mappings.arguable: AC-24 versus AC-3: row-level security decides and enforces in one mechanism, so these records could also be read as AC-3 evidence. They are listed here for what they add — the decision expressions read from the catalog, and a path (definer functions) on which the table's decision is bypassed — not as a second count of the same enforcement.

mappings.title: Account Management
statement: a. Define and document the types of accounts allowed and specifically prohibited for use within the system;
b. Assign account managers;
c. Require [Assignment: prerequisites and criteria] for group and role membership;
d. Specify:
1. Authorized users of the system;
2. Group and role membership; and
3. Access authorizations (i.e., privileges) and [Assignment: attributes (as required)] for each account;
e. Require approvals by [Assignment: personnel or roles] for requests to create accounts;
f. Create, enable, modify, disable, and remove accounts in accordance with [Assignment: policy, procedures, prerequisites, and criteria];
g. Monitor the use of accounts;
h. Notify account managers and [Assignment: personnel or roles] within:
1. [Assignment: time period] when accounts are no longer required;
2. [Assignment: time period] when users are terminated or transferred; and
3. [Assignment: time period] when system usage or need-to-know changes for an individual;
i. Authorize access to the system based on:
1. A valid access authorization;
2. Intended system usage; and
3. [Assignment: attributes (as required)];
j. Review accounts for compliance with account management requirements [Assignment: frequency];
k. Establish and implement a process for changing shared or group account authenticators (if deployed) when individuals are removed from the group; and
l. Align account management processes with personnel termination and transfer processes.
mappings.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, release 5.2.0 — NIST's OSCAL catalog, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/usnistgov/oscal-content/main/nist.gov/SP800-53/rev5/json/NIST_SP-800-53_rev5_catalog.json

artifacts.summary: WP0 inventory (run `20260922T234324Z-5695a4c3df2d`): 40 resources, 397 (resource, control) pairs, 50 policies, 88 SECURITY DEFINER functions (55 callable by a client role), 16 roles (5 with BYPASSRLS); row-level security enabled on 39 of 39 tables and forced on 0.

WP1 harness validation (run `20260922T234324Z-5695a4c3df2d`): 5 of 5 deliberately broken controls detected and 5 restored; over-privileged connections told intact from broken in 0 of 10 checks; the testing login can switch into service_role.

mappings.relevance: AC-2 is mostly an organizational process — account types, managers, prerequisites, approvals, monitoring, reviews, and removal aligned with personnel changes. Attest can speak only to a narrow technical part of it: which roles exist and what they may do, and what the database does when an account is deleted or a session expires.
demonstrates: WP0: 16 roles and their attributes, read from the catalog (5 hold BYPASSRLS); the role-attributes record re-reads them at assessment time (1 characterized).

Deleted account: 3 attempts held — after an account is deleted through Arc21's own function, its still-valid token reads nothing of the game-session data that survives the deletion; 11 were not measured, because the deletion leaves nothing of the account's own to target (C1).
Expired session: refused at the API boundary (1 effective).
doesNotDemonstrate: Any account-management process (AC-2 a–l): account types, managers, approvals, monitoring, reviews, or alignment with personnel changes. Arc21's accounts are self-service.
Token revocation: the deleted-account tests rely on the token staying valid until it expires, and show only that it reaches nothing.
Authentication itself (out of scope, brief §4).
limitations: 11 of 14 deleted-account attempts are not measured (C1).

mappings.title: Event Logging
statement: a. Identify the types of events that the system is capable of logging in support of the audit function: [Assignment: event types];
b. Coordinate the event logging function with other organizational entities requiring audit-related information to guide and inform the selection criteria for events to be logged;

c. Specify the following event types for logging within the system: [Assignment: organization-defined event types (subset of the event types defined in AU-2a.) along with the frequency of (or situation requiring) logging for each identified event type];
d. Provide a rationale for why the event types selected for logging are deemed to be adequate to support after-the-fact investigations of incidents; and
e. Review and update the event types selected for logging [Assignment: frequency].
mappings.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, release 5.2.0 — NIST's OSCAL catalog, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/usnistgov/oscal-content/main/nist.gov/SP800-53/rev5/json/NIST_SP-800-53_rev5_catalog.json

artifacts.summary: The author's J3/J4 rule applied to the 17 audit-absence resources (rubric/wp5-audit-scope.json): 13 require a trail, 3 excluded, 1 conditional.

mappings.relevance: AU-2 asks which events the system can log, which it must log, and why that selection is adequate for investigating incidents. The audit-trail family asked, for every High-tier resource, whether any record of who did what and when exists; the author's CP4 rule (J3) is, in effect, a written selection of what must be logged, with its reasons.
demonstrates: 33 records — 14 effective, 19 gap. Two structures log completely (private.game_commands and public.wallet_ledger), two partially (game events carry no actor; rate-limit events keep allowed attempts only), and seventeen High-tier resources log nothing.

Under the author's rule, 13 of those 17 require a trail and have none (A2, open); 3 are excluded as transient live state; 1 (public.wallets) depends on J4's conditions, which the evidence establishes only in part.
doesNotDemonstrate: Platform logging — PostgreSQL's own logs, pgaudit, the host's log drains — none was assessed, and none is visible to a catalog search.
Coordination with other functions, or a review cycle for the selection (AU-2 b, e).
limitations: The absence check is a heuristic over the catalogs (D3.55): a trail kept outside the schema, or written by a trigger that records by another route, would be missed.
mappings.provenance: ai_drafted — rationale, demonstrates, does-not-demonstrate, limitations and arguable notes drafted by AI (Claude) under Amendment A2; not written by the author

mappings.title: Content of Audit Records
statement: Ensure that audit records contain information that establishes the following:
a. What type of event occurred;
b. When the event occurred;
c. Where the event occurred;
d. Source of the event;
e. Outcome of the event; and
f. Identity of any individuals, subjects, or objects/entities associated with the event.
mappings.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, release 5.2.0 — NIST's OSCAL catalog, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/usnistgov/oscal-content/main/nist.gov/SP800-53/rev5/json/NIST_SP-800-53_rev5_catalog.json
mappings.subject: arc21
mappings.relevance: AU-3 lists what an audit record must establish: what happened, when, where, its source, its outcome, and who. The audit-trail family's content probes read the actor, action and time columns of each trail that exists.
demonstrates: 2 of 4 trails carry an actor, an action and a time (private.game_commands, public.wallet_ledger).

2 carry less: public.game_events has an action and a time but no actor — the author accepted the join to private.game_commands as the actor trail, conditionally (A3, J5), a join WP3 did not test and whose command rows are deleted with their account; public.rate_limit_events records allowed attempts only, so a refusal's outcome is never recorded (accepted by the author, J6).
doesNotDemonstrate: Where an event occurred and its source (AU-3 c, d): not examined.
Outcome, except implicitly: an entry exists because an action was allowed.
limitations: Content was read for existing rows of four trails; completeness across every event type was not measured.

mappings.title: Protection of Audit Information
statement: a. Protect audit information and audit logging tools from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion; and
b. Alert [Assignment: personnel or roles] upon detection of unauthorized access, modification, or deletion of audit information.
mappings.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, release 5.2.0 — NIST's OSCAL catalog, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/usnistgov/oscal-content/main/nist.gov/SP800-53/rev5/json/NIST_SP-800-53_rev5_catalog.json
mappings.subject: arc21
mappings.relevance: Not in the brief's minimum list; added because the evidence speaks to it directly. AU-9 asks that audit information be protected from unauthorized access, modification and deletion, and that such attempts raise an alert. The audit-trail family's immutability rows try to change, delete or truncate each trail as an ordinary client; the wallet family's ledger rows try the same on the privileged server path.
demonstrates: Client attempts to UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE a trail: 12 of 12 held.

Privileged path: the ledger's own triggers refused an UPDATE and a TRUNCATE (2 effective); 2 client attempts on the ledger were refused by the grant before its trigger could act and are not measured (C2).
doesNotDemonstrate: Protection from privileged roles in general: the owner and BYPASSRLS roles pass every policy (B1), and the ledger's guard permits a server-role DELETE by design, so an account's deletion can cascade to its entries (catalog reading, J4).
Alerting (AU-9 b): nothing alerts on an attempt.
limitations: Four trails exist to protect; the seventeen resources with no trail have nothing to protect (AU-2, AU-12).

mappings.title: Audit Record Generation
statement: a. Provide audit record generation capability for the event types the system is capable of auditing as defined in AU-2a on [Assignment: system components];
b. Allow [Assignment: personnel or roles] to select the event types that are to be logged by specific components of the system; and
c. Generate audit records for the event types defined in AU-2c that include the audit record content defined in AU-3.
mappings.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, release 5.2.0 — NIST's OSCAL catalog, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/usnistgov/oscal-content/main/nist.gov/SP800-53/rev5/json/NIST_SP-800-53_rev5_catalog.json
mappings.subject: arc21
mappings.relevance: AU-12 asks the system to generate audit records for the events AU-2 selects, with AU-3's content. The audit-trail family's existence probes read whether a trail actually holds records, and its absence probes whether any mechanism could generate one.
demonstrates: Records are generated for game commands and ledger entries (2 effective), and partially for game events and allowed rate-limit attempts (2 gap).
For 17 High-tier resources no mechanism generates any record (17 gap).
doesNotDemonstrate: A way to select which events are logged (AU-12 b): no such capability exists in the schema.
Record generation on platform components.
mappings.arguable: AU-2 versus AU-12: AU-2 is the decision about what must be logged; AU-12 is whether records are actually generated. The same audit-trail records bear on both; they are split so that an absence (AU-12) is not confused with the author's scope decision (AU-2).

artifacts.summary: WP4 drift run `20260925T042837Z-wp4`: 4 schema states (H1-009464c, 45 migrations; H2-4f9f7a6, 53 migrations; C-current, 59 migrations; T-controlled, 60 migrations), every state exit 0.
Arc21 read-only guard: fingerprint `13569cf0e2dd36c1…` identical before and after the official run; schema version `5695a4c3df2d` (59 migrations).

mappings.relevance: CM-3 is a process: decide which changes are controlled, review and approve them, record them, and monitor change activity. WP4 is a detective mechanism that could feed such a process: it rebuilds each schema state, inventories its controls, and classifies every difference.
demonstrates: Across 4 schema states, WP4 classified the history H1-009464c → C-current as 23 controls added, 9 removed, 4 definition changes and 4 attribute changes, with 0 approved questions going from pass to fail and 6 from fail to pass.
A table added with no row-level control in an Attest-only scratch state was reported on the run that added it (`public.attest_wp4_unprotected_notes`, not reachable by a client role today).
The assessed state's inventory, re-read by WP4, differs from the frozen CP1/CP3 inventory in 0 places.
Every run is bound to a content hash of the migration set, and every command fingerprints the Arc21 checkout before and after it runs.
doesNotDemonstrate: Any review, approval or change-control board (CM-3 b–d, g): Arc21 has no change-control process, and WP4 sees a change only after it was made.
Security impact analysis before a change (that is CM-4).
Continuous operation: WP4 ran on demand.
limitations: Historical states answer today's approved questions; a question that did not exist then is recorded as incompatible, never as a pass or a failure.
mappings.arguable: CM-3 versus CA-7: drift detection is the monitoring half of change control (CM-3 f) and the ongoing-assessment half of continuous monitoring (CA-7). It is listed under both; neither is met as a process.
mappings.provenance: ai_drafted — rationale, demonstrates, does-not-demonstrate, limitations and arguable notes drafted by AI (Claude) under Amendment A2; not written by the author

mappings.title: Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity
statement: a. Employ integrity verification tools to detect unauthorized changes to the following software, firmware, and information: [Assignment: organization-defined software, firmware, and information] ; and
b. Take the following actions when unauthorized changes to the software, firmware, and information are detected: [Assignment: organization-defined actions].
mappings.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, release 5.2.0 — NIST's OSCAL catalog, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/usnistgov/oscal-content/main/nist.gov/SP800-53/rev5/json/NIST_SP-800-53_rev5_catalog.json
mappings.subject: arc21
mappings.relevance: SI-7 asks for integrity verification tools that detect unauthorized changes to software, firmware and information. The wallet family tests something adjacent: whether the wallet's transactional design keeps the balance consistent with its ledger under concurrent and repeated calls, and whether the ledger refuses being rewritten.
demonstrates: 5 of 7 held: two overlapping deltas serialised and the balance equalled the ledger sum (F9.316); a repeated idempotency key credited once (F9.317); an over-debit was refused by a CHECK constraint (F9.318); UPDATE and TRUNCATE of the ledger were refused on the privileged path (F9.320, F9.322). 2 are not measured (C2).
doesNotDemonstrate: An integrity verification tool in SI-7's sense: nothing in Arc21 recomputes balances from the ledger or detects an unauthorized change after the fact; the one reconciliation was performed by the test itself, for one wallet.
Integrity of Arc21's software. (For Attest's own inputs, the harness hash, the migration-set hash and the Arc21 fingerprint are integrity checks of each run — of the assessment, not of Arc21.)
limitations: One wallet, fixed deltas, two concurrent sessions.
mappings.arguable: The brief proposed SI-7 for this family. It fits only in part: the family tests integrity-preserving mechanisms (serialisation, idempotency, a constraint, an append-only guard), not detection of unauthorized change. Recorded as partial rather than forced.
mappings.provenance: ai_drafted — rationale, demonstrates, does-not-demonstrate, limitations and arguable notes drafted by AI (Claude) under Amendment A2; not written by the author

Assessment of anything outside the data layer.

mappings.title: Continuous Monitoring
statement: Develop a system-level continuous monitoring strategy and implement continuous monitoring in accordance with the organization-level continuous monitoring strategy that includes:
a. Establishing the following system-level metrics to be monitored: [Assignment: system-level metrics];
b. Establishing [Assignment: frequencies] for monitoring and [Assignment: frequencies] for assessment of control effectiveness;
c. Ongoing control assessments in accordance with the continuous monitoring strategy;
d. Ongoing monitoring of system and organization-defined metrics in accordance with the continuous monitoring strategy;
e. Correlation and analysis of information generated by control assessments and monitoring;

mappings.title: § 11.10 Controls for closed systems.
statement: (d) Limiting system access to authorized individuals.
mappings.subject: arc21
mappings.relevance: Read against a study system, "limiting system access to authorized individuals" becomes the data-layer question WP3 asks: given an identity — or none, or a deleted account's, or an expired session's — what can it reach. The read, anonymous and Realtime families and the boundary cases put that question directly.
demonstrates: 134 Test IDs: 123 effective, 11 not measured (C1). No tested identity reached data the matrix forbids.
doesNotDemonstrate: That Arc21 is a closed system under Part 11 or keeps an electronic record any predicate rule requires (§11.3(b)(4), (6)): it is a personal game, not a regulated system.
Who the "authorized individuals" are: nothing authorizes anyone; accounts are self-service.
User authentication (out of scope, brief §4).
limitations: A study mapping: capped at partial whatever the results, because Part 11's subject — electronic records under FDA predicate rules — does not exist in Arc21.
mappings.arguable: §11.10(d) versus (g): (d) is who can get at the data at all; (g) is whether an authenticated user may alter a particular record or perform a particular operation. The reach-and-read families are listed under (d); the write, WITH CHECK, column and definer-function families under (g).

mappings.title: § 11.10 Controls for closed systems.
statement: (e) Use of secure, computer-generated, time-stamped audit trails to independently record the date and time of operator entries and actions that create, modify, or delete electronic records. Record changes shall not obscure previously recorded information. Such audit trail documentation shall be retained for a period at least as long as that required for the subject electronic records and shall be available for agency review and copying.
mappings.subject: arc21

artifacts.summary: The author's J3/J4 rule applied to the 17 audit-absence resources (rubric/wp5-audit-scope.json): 13 require a trail, 3 excluded, 1 conditional.

mappings.relevance: §11.10(e) asks for secure, computer-generated, time-stamped audit trails that independently record operator actions creating, modifying or deleting records, that never obscure earlier entries, and that are retained and available for review. The audit-trail family, and the ledger rows of the wallet family, examine exactly those properties where Arc21 has a trail.
demonstrates: Where Arc21 keeps a trail it has several of the properties: private.game_commands and public.wallet_ledger are computer-generated and time-stamped, ordinary clients cannot change or delete them, and the ledger refuses UPDATE for every role, so a correction is a new entry and earlier entries are not obscured (2 privileged-path records).
Where it does not, the gap is the finding: 19 audit-trail records are gaps, and the author's rule keeps 13 resources in scope for a trail they do not have (A2, open).
doesNotDemonstrate: Retention: game commands and ledger rows are deleted with their account (ON DELETE CASCADE), and a server role may delete ledger rows by design.
Independence of the trail from privileged operators, or availability for agency review and copying.
That Arc21 holds any electronic record within Part 11's scope.
limitations: A study mapping: capped at partial.

mappings.relevance: §11.10(g) asks for authority checks so that only authorized individuals can alter a record or perform the operation at hand. The write, WITH CHECK, column and definer-function families each put an authority check to that test.

The other four deficient records are the leaderboard item the author accepted as design intent (A1).

Device checks (that is §11.10(h), which is not mapped).

mappings.title: § 11.300 Controls for identification codes/passwords.
statement: Persons who use electronic signatures based upon use of identification codes in combination with passwords shall employ controls to ensure their security and integrity. Such controls shall include:
mappings.subject: arc21
mappings.relevance: §11.300 governs the identification codes and passwords behind electronic signatures: uniqueness, periodic revision, loss management for compromised tokens, transaction safeguards, and testing of token devices.
doesNotDemonstrate: Everything §11.300 asks. Authentication and credential management are outside Attest's scope (brief §4), Arc21 has no electronic signatures, and no Attest test examines identification codes, passwords or token issuance.
limitations: Not mapped: the brief listed §11.300 as a candidate, and the evidence does not support a mapping.
mappings.adjacent: Two results touch session tokens and are named here only so they are not mistaken for §11.300 evidence: an expired JWT is refused at the API boundary (B.suite.expired-session), and a deleted account's still-valid token reads nothing of what survives the deletion (B.331–.333). Neither is an identification-code or password control.
